CGPOWER.exposureFinding: The opposite of ADANIENT, and measurable. Semiconductors is a reported operating segment in consolidated accounts - OSAT and fabless design, identified separately under Ind AS 108 (page 176) - so the theme can be sized from the filing rather than asserted. FY26 semiconductor revenue of 502.77 crore is 4.0% of group revenue, its assets of 1,421.39 crore are 11.2% of group assets, and its capital expenditure of 330.33 crore is 42.5% of all group capex. A segment taking two fifths of the capital while earning four per cent of the revenue is the AI infrastructure thesis stated in the company's own numbers. External sales were nil in FY25, so this is the first year the segment earned anything, and it is loss-making at -107.86 crore against -22.39 the year before.

NETWEB.exposureFinding: The strongest theme figure any member discloses, and it is not segment reporting. The annual report carries a management table, "Revenue by Business Segment", putting AI Systems at 9,477.9 million, 43.4% of operating revenue, up from 1,693.8 million the year before. The audited accounts report one Ind AS 108 segment, Computer Servers, and make no segment disclosure. So the figure is company-disclosed and specific - far more than KAYNES or ADANIENT give - but it is not audited as a segment and cannot be tied to assets or capex. It belongs in the middle tier, not the top one.
NETWEB.exposureVerdict: A single audited segment, Computer Servers, but management discloses AI Systems at 43.4% of revenue - the most specific theme figure in the basket.

ADANIENT.exposureFinding: The open question is now answered, and the answer is no. There is no data centre segment in the consolidated segment table at page 339 - the segments are Integrated Resources Management, Mining Services, Commercial Mining, New Energy Ecosystem, Airport, Road, Copper and Others. AdaniConneX is a joint venture between AEL and EdgeConneX founded in 2021 (page 55) and is described as 'a joint venture of your Company' at page 155, so it is equity-accounted rather than consolidated: its revenue is in none of the 1,00,468.61 crore above, and its earnings appear only inside 'Share of Profit from Jointly Controlled Entities & Associates' of 257.18 crore, which covers every joint venture and associate together and is not broken out. So the data centre exposure of this member cannot be located in its financial statements at any size, and the 400 MW hyperscale order that admitted it sits in a vehicle whose results are not consolidated here.
ADANIENT.implication: The evidence that admitted ADANIENT is real, first-party and dated, and the admission is not withdrawn on this basis alone. What cannot be claimed is attribution: a reader cannot be shown what share of this company is the theme, because the filing does not say. Holding it for AI infrastructure means holding a diversified conglomerate whose reported revenue is mining, copper, airports and roads, for a stake in a joint venture. That is a decision for a reviewer, and it is recorded here rather than settled quietly.
ADANIENT.exposureVerdict: AdaniConneX is an equity-accounted joint venture and appears in no segment, so none of the reported revenue is data centre revenue.

measuredAgainstDerivation.finding: Upstox ratios are not on the annual statements. The P/E implies earnings per share of 266.24 against a filed FY26 figure of 221.63, which is a trailing twelve months that already includes the much stronger Q1 FY27. The P/B is 3.2% from the March 2026 book for the same reason - a more recent equity. So the basis mismatch is an as-of date, not consolidated versus standalone, and it matters far more for earnings than for book: equity compounds slowly, earnings jumped 157% year on year.

POWERINDIA.exposureFinding: No AI segment. Hitachi Energy India reports no separate data centre or AI line, so no share of revenue, assets or capex is attributable to the theme from the accounts. Its admitting evidence is different in kind from the others: individually sized orders - 56 units of 400 kV GIS, 12.8 km of busbar, 3x 220 kV transformers - which are attributable at the order level even though the segment is not. Order backlog of 29,555.30 crore is group-wide.
POWERINDIA.exposureVerdict: No AI segment; the admitting orders are individually sized but the backlog is group-wide.

attributionTiers.SEGMENT_REPORTED: The theme is a reported operating segment under Ind AS 108. Audited, and separable into revenue, result, assets and capex.
attributionTiers.MANAGEMENT_DISCLOSED: The company states a figure for the theme - a revenue vertical, a capacity share - outside its audited segment reporting. Company-disclosed and specific, but not audited as a segment, and it cannot be tied to assets or capex.
attributionTiers.NOT_ATTRIBUTABLE: Nothing separable. A single reporting segment absorbs the line, the exposure sits in an entity outside consolidation, or no figure for the theme is disclosed at all.
